items.status: FIXED — native-54, Order 54 (close at the merge)
items.title: `Option::take` / `Option::replace` over a receiver that lives in a cell natively — a module-level binding (`module_maybe.take()`), a field of one, a captured `mut` binding, a `Shared` view's field (`cell.write().maybe.take()`) — wrote a COPY taken out of the cell: the take answered the value and left the binding holding it (`Some(1)` natively, `None` on JS)
items.body: vilan-rust's `emit_intrinsic` counted only `mutates_its_receiver`'s eight intrinsics as writing their receiver, so `OptionTake`/`OptionReplace` rendered the receiver through the reading arm (`(MODULE.with(|cell| cell.get())).take()`, `(local.get()).take()`). They now count as mutating there: the receiver is `mutable_place` (the cell's `borrow_mut`, the arguments hoisted ahead of it, F30's shape). A plain local, a field of one and a `&mut self` field were places already and emit the same. Estate 0 (native emission of kolt's and the website's servers, every example entry and the corpus byte-identical). Pin `native_differential::an_option_take_through_a_cell_writes_the_cell_on_both_backends` (the base differed at 4 of 18 rows).

items.title: A callee that WRITES a module-level `mut` binding it was handed a loan of answers differently: `lent_and_grow(&module_items)` (the callee pushing into `module_items`, then reading `items.len()`) prints `1` on JS (the `&` is the binding's object) and `0` natively (a copy out of its `thread_local!` cell); `touch(&mut module_items)` (the callee pushing through the loan and then into `module_items` directly) prints `2` on JS and stops natively with the runtime's reentrancy sentence (the `&mut` holds the cell's borrow for the call)
items.body: F143's neighbour, past an argument list: the second path to the place is the CALLEE's body, not a later argument. Spec §6.4 rule 4 (no invalidating mutation under a live view) reads both as a write of the lent place while the loan is live — the checker cannot see it today because the write is in another function. The analyzer already has per-function write summaries (`function_reaches_an_in_place_write`, B634's closure-literal twin). Rec: a checker refusal at the call — lending a module-level `mut` binding (`&` or `&mut`, a receiver included) to a callee whose write summary reaches that binding — with the steer "copy it first: `let items = module_items; lent_and_grow(&items)`", estate counted first (expected 0: kolt and the website have no module-level `mut`, the corpus's four are scalar counters never lent). The alternative — a native VIEW of the cell held for the call — turns the `&` case into the runtime's reentrancy stop too, so it is no fix.

items.title: A by-value read of a module-level binding copied by rule 1 natively is copied TWICE: `has_N((MODULE_ITEMS.with(|cell| cell.get())).clone(), grow())` — `cell.get()` already answers a clone of the cell's value; the same for a field spine (`(MODULE_LOG.with(|cell| cell.get()).items).clone()` copies the whole struct, then the list again)
items.body: `copy_a_consumed_place_read` skips a read out of a boxed binding's cell or a `Shared` view ("a copy already, F62/F103") but not one out of a module binding's `thread_local!` cell, which is rendered `cell.get()` (a whole-value clone) — so wherever rule 1's copy applies (the JS `clone_sites` mark it beside a later writing argument, a non-last-use read) the value is cloned twice, and a field read clones the whole binding to read one field (F103's shape, unfixed for module roots). Rec: skip the second copy for a bare module read and a field/tuple-slot spine over one (an index spine still needs it: moving out of a `Vec` temporary's element is E0507), and read a field spine through the cell (`cell.read_with(|view| view.items.clone())`, F103's form) — native copy census rows move by the removed copies only; byte-identical output.
